ENGINEER QUESTION
Is this a possible leak or an instrumentation issue? Which pipeline section should an integrity engineer inspect first, and which sensors are unreliable?
ENGINEERING INTERPRETATION - MODEL-WRITTEN, FOR HUMAN REVIEW
Citation membership is checked; wording is not independently verified RCA. The checked evidence and safety limits below remain authoritative.
A leak is possible, not confirmed; instrumentation and operating changes remain unresolved alternatives. For inspection planning, prioritize review of the supported P1 interval in the checked numerical section, not a presumed leak point. No reviewed sensor is established as unreliable: P1-ST2-B has missing data but no flagged drift, spikes or peer disagreement. Anomalous readings are not themselves sensor faults, and the health review is partial.
Sources: claim-025, claim-026, claim-003, claim-031, claim-030, PROC-INSPECT-001
COMPETING CAUSES - NOT CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSES
leak (possible): A leak remains possible because the accepted pattern includes persistent anomalies at distinct stations and gateways. The historical comparison also shows localized pressure decreases rather than comparable changes at every compared sensor. Neither pressure patterns nor before/after association establish a leak; the supported interval is not a leak point.
Sources: claim-025, claim-028, claim-031, subsea_f8c95ce579d743aeaccb5b0546260b0a
operating change (not established): An operating change is not established, but cannot be excluded. The reviewed log excerpt contains no contemporaneous entry explaining the localized drop, yet explicitly omits potentially relevant activity and delayed entries. Corroborating operating records would help distinguish this alternative; absence of an entry is not evidence that no operation occurred.
Sources: LOG-COVERAGE-001, claim-029
instrumentation or telemetry (not established): Instrumentation or telemetry failure is not established. The reviewed anomalous taps have no flagged drift, spikes or peer disagreement, although P1-ST2-B has missing data. Support spans distinct gateways, but paired taps sharing a gateway are not independent corroboration. Shared-failure verification remains necessary; the bounded health review cannot establish reliability for unreviewed sensors.
Sources: claim-002, claim-003, claim-004, claim-005, claim-030, PROC-INSPECT-001
